svg.title: AWS Lambda
svg.desc: AWS Lambda. Functions as a service: code runs per event in managed execution environments that scale out with concurrency. Step 1, Where it sits: API Gateway waits on get-photo; S3 events reach make-thumbnail via SQS. Pay per request and GB-s. Step 2, Cold and warm starts: None idle: a microVM boots, code loads, init runs (cold start). An idle one runs only the handler. Step 3, Concurrency: One request per environment: 50 uploads/s × 0.8 s ≈ 40 at once, inside reserved concurrency 100. Step 4, Failures and limits: A bad photo: only its message is retried, then parked in the DLQ. Mind the 15 min and size limits.

g.text: API Gateway waits on get-photo; S3 events reach make-thumbnail via SQS. Pay per request and GB-s.
None idle: a microVM boots, code loads, init runs (cold start). An idle one runs only the handler.
One request per environment: 50 uploads/s × 0.8 s ≈ 40 at once, inside reserved concurrency 100.
A bad photo: only its message is retried, then parked in the DLQ. Mind the 15 min and size limits.
env A · warm start: handler only
env B · cold start: init, then handler
One square = one execution environment of make-thumbnail.
Lambda adds them as work arrives and removes idle ones later.
THREE WAYS TO INVOKE A FUNCTION
Synchronous: API Gateway calls Invoke and waits for get-photo’s answer. Asynchronous: S3, SNS or EventBridge hand the event to
Lambda’s internal queue and get 202 at once. Polling: an event source mapping reads thumbnail-jobs and invokes make-thumbnail.
No servers to patch or size: you pay per request plus GB-seconds of run time (memory × duration), and nothing for idle time.
An environment runs one request at a time. Request 2 finds env A idle: Lambda thaws it and runs only the handler, a warm start.
Request 3 finds none free: Lambda boots a Firecracker microVM, loads the code, starts the runtime and runs the init code
(SDK clients, config), a cold start that is billed and slower. Idle environments are frozen, then removed: reuse is never promised.
50 uploads a second × 0.8 s each ≈ 40 environments at once. The SQS mapping starts with 5 concurrent invokes and adds up to 300 a minute.
Reserved concurrency 100 caps make-thumbnail and sets 100 aside from the account’s 1,000 per Region. Past a limit: throttled (429).
Provisioned concurrency keeps 2 get-photo environments initialised (billed while on); SnapStart restores Java, Python, .NET from a snapshot.
The handler reports the failed message: 9 are deleted, 1 comes back
after the visibility timeout. After 5 receives SQS moves it to the DLQ.
Delivery is at least once, so the handler must be idempotent.
15 min per invoke · memory 128–10,240 MB, CPU in proportion
payload 6 MB sync, 1 MB async · /tmp up to 10,240 MB
Long or steady, busy work is often cheaper in containers.
